title: Reliability Runbook Garden Canvas - Initiative Brief
body:
Purpose:

A practical, cross-team plan to build, validate, and operate a curated "Runbook Garden" for model-serving services and platform components that maps to SLOs and error budget experiments. This doc captures the initiative canvas, early sprint backlog, owner matrix, communication cadence, and things we still need to decide. Intended to be a working artifact for 30/60/90 day sprints.

Scope (what is in/out):
- In scope: runbooks for model-serving inference path, autoscaler, KV cache, routing fallback, and customer-facing endpoint health.
- Out of scope: data-plane encryption policies, billing pipelines, infra procurement.

Goals (measurable):
- Publish 1st-runbook set for 6 critical services within 45 days.
- Each runbook tied to at least one SLO and a single error-budget remediation path.
- Reduce mean time to mitigation (MTTM) for P1 latency incidents by 30% in Q2 (pilot teams).
- Run 3 error-budget experiments and capture impact on latency/cost.

Success metrics / signals:
- # published runbooks (target 6 -> 12)
- SLO coverage percentage for platform-critical routes (target 85%)
- Average operator time to corrective action on simulated incidents (baseline -> -30%)
- Number of times an automated fallback invoked successfully in canary (target >= 95%)

Stakeholders / RACI (high level):
- Product: Maya Li (owner for routing fallback SLOs) - consult on policy
- Platform Eng: Priya Shah (initiative lead) - accountable for delivery
- Serving Runtime: Jonah Becker - responsible for KV/cache and kernel-selection runbooks
- SRE: Ethan Ramirez - responsible for runbook validation and SLO experiments
- Customer Success: Sana Patel - informed; will validate runbooks for customer-facing scenarios

Workstreams & early backlog (30-day priorities):
1) Runbook templates + minimal required telemetry
   - deliverable: canonical template + example for inference-route
   - tasks: audit current docs, add telemetry checklist, add runbook ownership fields
   - owners: Priya, Jonah

2) SLO mapping and canonical definitions
   - deliverable: SLO spreadsheet with objective, target, measurement query, burn-rate thresholds
   - tasks: define SLA->SLO mapping for top 10 endpoints, finalize burn-rate actions
   - owners: Maya, Ethan

3) Experiment harness for error-budget drills
   - deliverable: scriptable chaos harness for latency/injection tests + playbook for validation
   - tasks: build smoke tests, run in staging, collect signals, iterate
   - owners: Ethan, Jonah

4) Communication & activation lanes
   - deliverable: activation matrix (who calls war-room, who escalates to infra) + Slack shortcuts
   - tasks: define oncall runbook shortcuts, update alert routing policies, document escalation timing
   - owners: Priya, Sana

Milestones / Timeline (tentative):
- Week 1-2: Runbook template + SLO spreadsheet seed + stakeholder kickoff
- Week 3-4: Publish first 3 runbooks, instrumentation gaps triaged, first chaos smoke
- Week 6: Error-budget experiment #1 + retro, update runbooks based on findings
- Week 8-10: Expand runbook set to 6 services, rolling canary with fallback policies

Runbook quality checklist (minimum):
- short description of failure modes
- measurement queries (prometheus/tempo) + dashboard link
- immediate mitigation steps (3 lines to triage, 5 lines to remediate)
- verified rollback/fallback instruction with test steps
- post-incident entries: corrective action owner and ETA

Observability & instrumentation tasks (key):
- Ensure p95/p99/latency histograms exported for each route
- Add KV-cache hit/miss metrics + correlation with request latency
- Tag traces with model-version, route-id, and customer-tier
- Add synthetic checks for end-to-end response and structured response validation

Communication plan:
- Weekly 30m sync (Platform + SRE + Serving Runtime + Prod Eng) — Wednesdays 11am PT
- Biweekly demo for GTM/Customer Success — 1st & 3rd Fridays
- Incident activation playbook published to confluence + pinned channel snippets

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: telemetry gaps slow runbook validation -> Mitigation: minimal telemetry checklist and temporary synthetic tests
- Risk: runbook ownership ambiguity -> Mitigation: require explicit owner field and SLA for updates (30d)
- Risk: experiment causes customer regressions -> Mitigation: run in staging, small canary percentages, automatic rollback

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Which teams authorize runbook gating for production rollouts? (proposal: Platform Eng + SRE sign-off)
- What burn-rate threshold triggers automated throttling vs. human intervention? (options: 2x burn for 5m -> auto throttle)
- How do we capture runbook doc changes as code? (RFC: small repo and PR process; infra approves templates)

Immediate action items (today / next 48h):
- Priya: spin up runbook repo and push initial template (TODO: add CODEOWNERS)
- Jonah: audit current telemetry on KV cache and list gaps
- Ethan: prototype chaos script for 95th percentile latency injection in staging
- Maya: finalize SLO measurement queries for top 5 routes

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- "Runbook Garden": think of runbooks as curated plants — some need pruning, some need irrigation (telemetry).
- consider a lightweight badge system: bronze/silver/gold runbook readiness; surface in Console for teams.
- long-term: tie runbook maturity to release gates in the deployment pipeline (can block rollouts if critical SLOs uncovered)

Appendix: references and quick links:
- runbook template draft: github:infra/runbook-templates/blob/main/template.md
- SLO spreadsheet (working): confluence:SLO-MAP-2026
- smoke harness: github:infra/chaos-scripts/tree/runbook-experiments

End of brief. Keep this doc alive — will iterate into a Confluence charter after 60d once pilot results in hand.
